title: The Catholic Church
hookLine: the largest church, united with the Bishop of Rome, with the Mass at its heart

lines: THE SUN MOVES AROUND THE WORLD.
cards: Sunday morning moves around the planet. As the sun rises over a village in the Philippines, a bell rings and a priest lifts a round white host. An hour or so later, the same thing in Vietnam.

Then in India, in Nigeria, in Poland, in Brazil at a packed six o'clock evening Mass, in a little church in Ohio with forty people and a slightly out-of-tune organ. The languages change. The music changes.
In the Latin rite, the words are nearly the same, translated from one Latin book. This is the largest Christian church on earth.

teach.h: UNITED WITH THE BISHOP OF ROME.
teach.b: The Catholic Church is the communion of churches united with the bishop of Rome, the pope.
Catholics trace that role to Peter, and to Jesus's words to him in Matthew: "thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church." The name Peter means rock.
Catholics understand the pope as Peter's successor, a sign and servant of the church's unity. Other Christians read that verse differently, some saying the rock is Peter's faith, or Christ himself.
It's a very old conversation, and it still goes on. At the heart of Catholic life is the Mass.
Catholics believe that in the Mass the bread and wine truly become the body and blood of Christ, and they call the Eucharist the source and summit of the Christian life.

teach.h: ITE, MISSA EST: GO, IT IS THE DISMISSAL.
teach.b: The word Mass comes from the last Latin line of the old service: ite, missa est, go, it is the dismissal. Missa comes from the verb to send: the service ends by sending people out.
Around the Mass sit seven sacraments, from baptism to the anointing of the sick, marking a life from birth to death.
And the church isn't only Roman.

teach.h: UPON THIS ROCK I WILL BUILD MY CHURCH.
teach.b: Beside the large Latin church there are more than twenty Eastern Catholic churches, Ukrainian, Maronite, Melkite, Chaldean and others, with their own liturgies and customs, some with married priests, all in communion with the pope.
Catholic itself means universal, from a Greek phrase, according to the whole. We'll come back to that word later on the path.

how: Catholics are asked to attend Mass every Sunday and on holy days of obligation, and many also pray the rosary, go to confession, and honor Mary and the saints.

games.q: the old Latin Mass is over. the priest turns to the people with one last line. what does it say?
games.why: ite, missa est: go, it is the dismissal. the service ends by sending people out, and it gave the Mass its name.

practice: Think of a Catholic you know, or knew, a grandmother, a coworker, a friend from school, and one thing they loved: the rosary in their pocket, a saint they talked to, Midnight Mass at Christmas, the smell of the church.

Hold that one thing in mind with respect, and if you pray, pray for them, and for the Catholic Church. If you don't know any Catholics, picture that little church in Ohio, forty people and an out-of-tune organ.

wordCard.voice: Missa. The Latin word the Mass gets its name from, meaning the sending, the dismissal at the end of the service.

orig.note: Latin: the dismissal, from mittere, to send; the Mass's last line is, ite, missa est. The root of the word Mass.

carryVoice: Your line: universal. One Mass, many languages, from the Philippines to Ohio. See you tomorrow.
